records.source: בִּשְׁנַ֛ת שְׁמוֹנֶ֥ה עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ יָרָבְעָ֑ם וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ אֲבִיָּ֖ה עַל־יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: In [the] year eighteen of the king Jeroboam, and reigned Abijah over Judah.
pieces: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah became king over Judah.

L.1: In [the] eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah reigned over Judah.

R.1: Abijah became king of Judah. It was the eighteenth year that Jeroboam had been king of Israel.

decisions.choice: the opening of Abijah's reign as in 1 Kings 15:1
decisions.reason: This verse and the next retell 1 Kings 15:1-2. Two things differ: Chronicles leaves out "son of Nebat" after Jeroboam's name, and it calls the king Abijah where Kings calls him Abijam. This is the only time Chronicles dates the start of a reign by the year of a king of Israel.

decisions.choice: Abijah: the same king 1 Kings 15:1-8 calls Abijam
decisions.reason: Chronicles calls Rehoboam's son Abijah (12:16; 13:1-23), a name that means "my father is Yahweh". Kings calls him Abijam throughout. The two forms name the same man; each book's form is kept.

decisions.choice: reigned: became king
decisions.reason: With a date the verb marks the start of the reign, as in 1 Kings 15:1.

decisions.choice: two sentences, the date second, naming Israel
decisions.reason: Readable splits the formula into two sentences, as in 1 Kings 15:1, and names Israel so the reader knows which kingdom Jeroboam ruled.

records.heading: Abijah king of Judah

records.source: שָׁל֣וֹשׁ שָׁנִ֗ים מָלַךְ֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ מִיכָיָ֥הוּ בַת־אוּרִיאֵ֖ל מִן־גִּבְעָ֑ה וּמִלְחָמָ֥ה הָיְתָ֛ה בֵּ֥ין אֲבִיָּ֖ה וּבֵ֥ין יָרָבְעָֽם׃
records.gloss: Three years he reigned in Jerusalem, and [the] name of his mother [was] Micaiah daughter of Uriel from Gibeah. And war was between Abijah and between Jeroboam.
pieces: He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Micaiah daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

L.2: Three years he reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [was] Micaiah daughter of Uriel from Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

R.2: He ruled in Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Micaiah, the daughter of Uriel from Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

decisions.choice: Micaiah daughter of Uriel of Gibeah: kept as the Hebrew text has it
alternatives: Maacah daughter of Uriel of Gibeah
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 15:2 names Abijah's mother "Maacah daughter of Abishalom", and 2 Chronicles 11:20-22 says Rehoboam married "Maacah daughter of Absalom" and made her son Abijah his heir. Some ancient translations read Maacah here too. Micaiah may be a slip in copying for Maacah, since the names look alike, or another form of her name. If Uriel of Gibeah was her father, "daughter of Absalom" may mean granddaughter, as "daughter" can name a female descendant. The Hebrew text here is followed.

decisions.choice: war between Abijah and Jeroboam: as in 1 Kings 15:7
decisions.reason: Kings gives this line at the close of Abijam's reign (1 Kings 15:7) and tells nothing more of the war. Chronicles places it here and goes on to tell of one battle in it (verses 3-20).

decisions.choice: He reigned three years; He ruled ... for three years
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 15:2, Balanced and Readable start with the subject; Literal keeps the Hebrew order, which puts the number first.

records.source: וַיֶּאְסֹ֨ר אֲבִיָּ֜ה אֶת־הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה בְּחַ֨יִל֙ גִּבּוֹרֵ֣י מִלְחָמָ֔ה אַרְבַּע־מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֖לֶף אִ֣ישׁ בָּח֑וּרסוְיָרָבְעָ֗ם עָרַ֤ךְ עִמּוֹ֙ מִלְחָמָ֔ה בִּשְׁמוֹנֶ֨ה מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֛לֶף אִ֥ישׁ בָּח֖וּר גִּבּ֥וֹר חָֽיִל׃ס
records.gloss: And bound Abijah the battle with an army of mighty [men] of war, four hundred thousand man chosen, and Jeroboam arranged with him battle with eight hundred thousand man chosen, mighty [men] of strength.
pieces: Abijah went into battle with an army of warriors, 400,000 chosen men, and Jeroboam drew up his battle lines against him with 800,000 chosen men, mighty warriors.

L.3: And Abijah joined the battle with an army of mighty [men] of war, 400,000 chosen men, and Jeroboam drew up [the] battle against him with 800,000 chosen men, mighty [men] of valor.

R.3: Abijah went to war with an army of 400,000 of his best fighting men. Jeroboam lined up 800,000 of his best men to fight against him. They were brave warriors.

decisions.choice: bound the battle: began the fight, went to war
decisions.reason: To "bind" a battle is to join it or set it going, as a cart is hitched to its animals (compare 1 Kings 20:14). Jeroboam answers by drawing up his lines against Abijah.

decisions.choice: four hundred thousand ... eight hundred thousand: the size of the numbers
decisions.reason: The word for "thousand" can also name a military unit, which would make these armies far smaller; see the note at Numbers 1:21. The text gives Jeroboam twice Abijah's force, and the story turns on that: Judah wins against the odds.

decisions.choice: chosen men: picked soldiers
decisions.reason: The word means men chosen for their fitness, the best fighters of each side (Judges 20:15-16; 1 Samuel 24:3).

decisions.choice: numerals: 400,000 and 800,000
decisions.reason: Numbers above ninety-nine are written as numerals at every level, as the style of this translation sets.

decisions.choice: a separate sentence for "mighty men of valor"
decisions.reason: Readable says "best fighting men" for the chosen soldiers and puts the closing description of Jeroboam's army in a short sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: mighty [men] of valor (Literal); mighty warriors (Balanced); brave warriors (Readable)
decisions.reason: One wording for this phrase at each level, as in 1 Chronicles 7:2 and through 2 Chronicles (14:7; 17:13-17; 25:6; 26:12; 32:21).

records.source: וַיָּ֣קָם אֲבִיָּ֗ה מֵעַל֙ לְהַ֣ר צְמָרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שְׁמָע֖וּנִי יָרָבְעָ֥ם וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And stood Abijah on top of Mount Zemaraim, which [is] in [the] hill country of Ephraim, and he said, Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel!
pieces: Abijah stood up on Mount Zemaraim, in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, "Listen to me, Jeroboam and all Israel!

L.4: And Abijah stood up on top of Mount Zemaraim, which [is] in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, "Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel!

R.4: Abijah stood on top of Mount Zemaraim in the hill country of Ephraim and called out, "Listen to me, Jeroboam and all you people of Israel!

decisions.choice: Mount Zemaraim: a height near the border between the two kingdoms
decisions.reason: A town Zemaraim is listed in Benjamin near Bethel (Joshua 18:22). The hill country of Ephraim reached south into that area, so Abijah stood near the border, in sight of Jeroboam's army.

decisions.choice: all Israel: the northern kingdom and its army
decisions.reason: Here "Israel" means the ten tribes who followed Jeroboam (10:16-19), whose army stood facing Judah. Abijah speaks to them across the lines.

decisions.choice: the speech runs from here to verse 12
decisions.reason: Abijah's speech fills verses 4-12. It is one of the speeches found only in Chronicles, and it sets out why Judah's cause is the LORD's.

decisions.choice: called out; all you people of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says "called out", since Abijah spoke from a height to an army, and "all you people of Israel" so that "Israel" is heard as the people he addresses.

records.heading: Abijah's speech on Mount Zemaraim

records.source: הֲלֹ֤א לָכֶם֙ לָדַ֔עַת כִּ֞י יְהוָ֣ה׀אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל נָתַ֨ן מַמְלָכָ֧ה לְדָוִ֛יד עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְעוֹלָ֑ם ל֥וֹ וּלְבָנָ֖יו בְּרִ֥ית מֶֽלַח׃ס
records.gloss: [Is it] not for you to know that Yahweh God of Israel gave kingship to David over Israel forever, to him and to his sons, a covenant of salt?
pieces: Should you not know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, gave the kingship over Israel to David and his sons forever by a covenant of salt?

L.5: Is it not for you to know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel gave the kingship over Israel to David forever, to him and to his sons, [by] a covenant of salt?

R.5: You ought to know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, gave David and his descendants the right to rule over Israel forever. He made a covenant of salt with them, a covenant that will never end.

decisions.choice: is it not for you to know?: you ought to know
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "yes". Abijah reminds the northern tribes of something they should already know.

decisions.choice: a covenant of salt: a covenant meant to last for ever
decisions.reason: Salt keeps food from spoiling, and eating salt together sealed a bond between people. The phrase is used of the priests' share in Numbers 18:19, and salt went with every offering as "the salt of the covenant of your God" (Leviticus 2:13). Abijah uses it of Yahweh's lasting covenant with David.

decisions.choice: kingship over Israel to David and his sons forever: the promise of 2 Samuel 7
decisions.reason: Yahweh promised David that his house and his kingdom would stand forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16; 1 Chronicles 17:11-14). "Israel" here is all twelve tribes, so Abijah argues that the northern kingdom broke away from the line Yahweh had chosen.

decisions.choice: his sons: his descendants
decisions.reason: The word means sons and, more widely, a man's line after him.

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question; covenant of salt explained
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies, and adds "a covenant that will never end" to say what a covenant of salt means, as in Numbers 18:19.

records.source: וַיָּ֨קָם֙ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֔ט עֶ֖בֶד שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בֶן־דָּוִ֑יד וַיִּמְרֹ֖ד עַל־אֲדֹנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And arose Jeroboam son of Nebat, servant of Solomon son of David, and rebelled against his lord.
pieces: Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat, an official of Solomon son of David, rose and turned in revolt against his own master.

L.6: Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his lord.

R.6: But Jeroboam son of Nebat rose up and rebelled against his master. He had been one of the officials of Solomon son of David.

decisions.choice: Jeroboam's rebellion: told in 1 Kings 11:26-40
decisions.reason: Jeroboam had been in charge of the labor gangs of the house of Joseph under Solomon (1 Kings 11:26-28). He rebelled against the king and fled to Egypt, and came back to lead the northern tribes after Solomon's death (10:2-3).

decisions.choice: servant of Solomon: a royal official
decisions.reason: Here the word for servant names a man in the king's service, an official (1 Kings 11:26), not a household slave. Abijah stresses that Jeroboam rose against the master he served.

decisions.choice: his lord: Solomon
decisions.reason: The word is plural in form, as titles of honor often are, but it means one master, Solomon.

decisions.choice: an official; one of the officials; his master
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "official" for a king's servant, as in 1 Kings 11:26, and "master" for the man he served. Readable puts Jeroboam's office in a sentence of its own.

records.source: וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ עָלָ֗יו אֲנָשִׁ֤ים רֵקִים֙ בְּנֵ֣י בְלִיַּ֔עַל וַיִּֽתְאַמְּצ֖וּ עַל־רְחַבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וּרְחַבְעָ֗ם הָ֤יָה נַ֨עַר֙ וְרַךְ־לֵבָ֔ב וְלֹ֥א הִתְחַזַּ֖ק לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And gathered around him men empty, sons of worthlessness, and they strengthened themselves against Rehoboam son of Solomon, and Rehoboam was young and tender of heart, and not he strengthened himself before them.
pieces: Worthless men, scoundrels, gathered around him and stood firm against Rehoboam son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and timid and could not hold his own against them.

L.7: And empty men, sons of worthlessness, gathered around him and made themselves strong against Rehoboam son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and tender of heart, and he did not show himself strong before them.

R.7: Worthless, wicked men joined him and stood up against Rehoboam son of Solomon. Rehoboam was young and unsure of himself, and he was not strong enough to stand up to them.

decisions.choice: empty men: men of no worth or principle
decisions.reason: "Empty" men are reckless men with nothing to lose, the kind who gathered around Abimelech and Jephthah (Judges 9:4; 11:3).

decisions.choice: sons of worthlessness: scoundrels
decisions.reason: The word means worthlessness or wickedness, as in "a worthless man" said of Sheba, who led the northern tribes away from David (2 Samuel 20:1). "Sons of" it are men marked by it (1 Samuel 2:12).

decisions.choice: young and tender of heart: inexperienced and timid
decisions.reason: Rehoboam was forty-one when he became king (12:13), so "young" here means inexperienced rather than a boy (compare 1 Kings 3:7). A "tender" heart is a soft or fearful one: he lacked the firmness to stand against them.

decisions.choice: made themselves strong ... did not show himself strong: the same verb set against itself
decisions.reason: Two forms of the verb for being strong play against each other: the rebels asserted themselves, and Rehoboam could not. The account in chapter 10 also tells of Rehoboam's harsh answer to the people and says the turn of events came from God (10:15); Abijah gives his side's view.

decisions.choice: worthless men, scoundrels; timid; unsure of himself
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the two Hebrew phrases for the rebels into plain words, and say what "tender of heart" means.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀אַתֶּ֣ם אֹֽמְרִ֗ים לְהִתְחַזֵּק֙ לִפְנֵי֙ מַמְלֶ֣כֶת יְהוָ֔ה בְּיַ֖ד בְּנֵ֣י דָוִ֑יד וְאַתֶּם֙ הָמ֣וֹן רָ֔ב וְעִמָּכֶם֙ עֶגְלֵ֣י זָהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם יָרָבְעָ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And now you [are] saying to strengthen yourselves before [the] kingdom of Yahweh in [the] hand of [the] sons of David, and you [are] a multitude great, and with you [are] calves of gold which made for you Jeroboam for gods.
pieces: And now you mean to stand against the kingdom of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that David's sons hold. You are a vast horde, and with you are the golden calves Jeroboam made to be your gods.

L.8: And now you are saying [you will] show yourselves strong before the kingdom of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the hand of the sons of David, and you [are] a great multitude, and with you [are] calves of gold that Jeroboam made for you as gods.

R.8: Now you think you can fight against the kingdom that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has put in the hands of David's descendants. There are very many of you, and you have the gold statues of young bulls that Jeroboam made to be your gods.

decisions.choice: you are saying: you think, you mean to
decisions.reason: To "say" here is to say to oneself, to intend (compare 1 Samuel 30:6; 2 Samuel 21:16). The same verb for showing strength was used in verse 7.

decisions.choice: the kingdom of Yahweh in the hand of the sons of David
decisions.reason: The kingdom belongs to Yahweh, and David's line rules it on his behalf (1 Chronicles 17:14; 28:5; 29:23). So to fight David's heirs is to fight Yahweh, as verse 12 will say.

decisions.choice: calves of gold that Jeroboam made for you as gods
decisions.reason: Jeroboam made two golden calves and set them up at Bethel and Dan (1 Kings 12:28-29). "With you" may mean the calves were carried with the army, or only that they are the gods the northern tribes now have; the text does not say which.

decisions.choice: gold statues of young bulls
decisions.reason: Readable explains "calves" as in 1 Kings 12:28.

decisions.choice: a vast horde
decisions.reason: Balanced says "horde" for the word that means a noisy crowd or throng, since Abijah speaks of a huge army.

records.source: הֲלֹ֤א הִדַּחְתֶּם֙ אֶת־כֹּהֲנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹ֖ן וְהַלְוִיִּ֑ם וַתַּעֲשׂ֨וּ לָכֶ֤ם כֹּהֲנִים֙ כְּעַמֵּ֣י הָאֲרָצ֔וֹת כָּל־הַבָּ֗א לְמַלֵּ֨א יָד֜וֹ בְּפַ֤ר בֶּן־בָּקָר֙ וְאֵילִ֣ם שִׁבְעָ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה כֹהֵ֖ן לְלֹ֥א אֱלֹהִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: [Have] not you driven out [the] priests of Yahweh, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and you made for yourselves priests like [the] peoples of the lands? Whoever comes to fill his hand with a bull, a son of [the] herd, and rams seven, and he becomes a priest of not gods.
pieces: Did you not drive out the priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Aaron's sons, together with the Levites, and make your own priests as the peoples of other lands do? Anyone who comes to consecrate himself with a young bull and seven rams becomes a priest of what are no gods.

L.9: Have you not driven out the priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made priests for yourselves like the peoples of the lands? Whoever comes to fill his hand with a young bull of the herd and seven rams becomes a priest of no gods.

R.9: You drove out the priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who are Aaron's descendants, and you drove out the Levites. Then you chose your own priests, just as the people of other nations do. Anyone who comes with a young bull and seven rams to make himself a priest becomes a priest of gods that are not gods at all.

decisions.choice: you drove out the priests ... and made priests for yourselves
decisions.reason: Jeroboam made priests from all sorts of people who were not Levites (1 Kings 12:31; 13:33), and the priests and Levites of the north left their lands and went to Judah (11:13-15).

decisions.choice: to fill his hand: to be ordained as priest
decisions.reason: To "fill the hand" of a priest is to install him in office (Exodus 28:41; 29:9; 1 Kings 13:33). Here the man fills his own hand: he makes himself a priest.

decisions.choice: a young bull and seven rams: the offering brought to be ordained
decisions.reason: Aaron's ordination called for one young bull and two rams (Exodus 29:1). The larger offering here may have been what Jeroboam's shrines asked of anyone who wanted to be a priest; Abijah's point is that anyone who paid it could serve.

decisions.choice: a priest of no gods: of gods that are not real
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of idols in Jeremiah 2:11 and 5:7, and Hosea says of the calf of Samaria, "it is not God" (Hosea 8:6). Abijah says the calves are not gods at all.

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question; the verse in three sentences
decisions.reason: Readable states as fact what Abijah asks as a question that expects "yes", and repeats "drove out" so the Levites are clearly included.

decisions.choice: consecrate himself; make himself a priest; peoples of other lands
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom of the filled hand means (m2). They add "other" to "lands", since the phrase means the nations around Israel.

records.source: וַאֲנַ֛חְנוּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ וְלֹ֣א עֲזַבְנֻ֑הוּ וְכֹ֨הֲנִ֜ים מְשָׁרְתִ֤ים לַֽיהוָה֙ בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֔ן וְהַלְוִיִּ֖ם בַּמְלָֽאכֶת׃
records.gloss: And we, Yahweh [is] our God, and not we have forsaken him, and priests serving Yahweh [are the] sons of Aaron, and the Levites [are] in the work.
pieces: But we have {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as our God, and we have not forsaken {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Sons of Aaron serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as priests, and the Levites are at their work.

L.10: But as for us, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] our God, and we have not forsaken {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; and the priests ministering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [are] sons of Aaron, and the Levites [are] at the work.

R.10: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is our God, and we have not turned away from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. The priests who serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} are descendants of Aaron, and the Levites do the work they were given.

decisions.choice: and we: but as for us
decisions.reason: The word "we" stands first, setting Judah against the northern tribes Abijah has just described (verses 8-9).

decisions.choice: we have not forsaken him: we have kept faith with Yahweh
decisions.reason: To forsake Yahweh is to leave his worship and his covenant (7:19-22; 12:1, 5). Abijah claims that Judah has not done so, and verse 11 says how.

decisions.choice: the Levites at the work: in their appointed service
decisions.reason: The Levites helped the priests in the service of the temple (1 Chronicles 23:28-32). Abijah names the two orders the Law set apart, against Jeroboam's priests of verse 9.

decisions.choice: turned away from; do the work they were given
decisions.reason: Readable says "turned away from" for "forsaken" and spells out that the Levites' work was assigned to them.

records.source: וּמַקְטִרִ֣ים לַיהוָ֡ה עֹל֣וֹת בַּבֹּֽקֶר־בַּבֹּ֣קֶר וּבָעֶֽרֶב־בָּעֶ֣רֶב וּקְטֹֽרֶת־סַמִּים֩ וּמַעֲרֶ֨כֶת לֶ֜חֶם עַל־הַשֻּׁלְחָ֣ן הַטָּה֗וֹר וּמְנוֹרַ֨ת הַזָּהָ֤ב וְנֵרֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ לְבָעֵר֙ בָּעֶ֣רֶב בָּעֶ֔רֶב כִּֽי־שֹׁמְרִ֣ים אֲנַ֔חְנוּ אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְאַתֶּ֖ם עֲזַבְתֶּ֥ם אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And making smoke to Yahweh burnt offerings in the morning, in the morning, and in the evening, in the evening, and incense of spices, and row of bread on the table the pure, and [the] lampstand of the gold and its lamps to burn in the evening, in the evening, for keeping [are] we [the] charge of Yahweh our God, and you have forsaken him.
pieces: Every morning and every evening they burn burnt offerings and fragrant incense to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The bread is set out in rows on the pure table, and the lamps on the golden lampstand are lit every evening. For we are keeping the charge of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, but you have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.11: And they make smoke to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [with] burnt offerings morning by morning and evening by evening, and incense of spices; and the row of bread [is] on the pure table, and the lampstand of gold and its lamps [are there] to burn evening by evening. For we keep the charge of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, but you have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.11: Every morning and every evening they offer burnt offerings and burn sweet-smelling incense to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They set out the bread in rows on the table of pure gold, and every evening they light the lamps on the gold lampstand. We do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God has given us to do, but you have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings and incense every morning and evening
decisions.reason: The Law set a burnt offering every morning and evening (Exodus 29:38-42; Numbers 28:3-8) and incense morning and evening (Exodus 30:7-8). The doubled "in the morning, in the morning" means every morning.

decisions.choice: the row of bread and the lampstand: the daily service inside the holy place
decisions.reason: Bread was set in rows on the table before Yahweh (Leviticus 24:5-9), and the lamps were kept burning from evening to morning (Exodus 27:20-21; Leviticus 24:2-4). Solomon had made ten lampstands (4:7); Abijah speaks of the service as a whole.

decisions.choice: the pure table: the table of pure gold
decisions.reason: The table is called "the pure table" in Leviticus 24:6, and Exodus 31:8 speaks of "the pure lampstand": both were covered with or made of pure gold (Exodus 25:24, 31). The word can also mean ritually clean, and the two senses go together here.

decisions.choice: keep the charge of Yahweh: carry out the duties Yahweh has set
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of the duties of priests and Levites at the sanctuary (Leviticus 8:35; Numbers 3:7-8). Judah does what Yahweh requires; the north has forsaken him.

decisions.choice: is set out ... are lit; they set out ... they light
decisions.reason: The Hebrew lists the bread and the lampstand after the verb "make smoke", which fits only the offerings and incense. Balanced and Readable give each item its own verb.

decisions.choice: the table of pure gold; we do what ... has given us to do
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the pure table" was (m3) and what keeping the charge means (m4).

records.source: וְהִנֵּה֩ עִמָּ֨נוּ בָרֹ֜אשׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֧ים׀וְכֹהֲנָ֛יו וַחֲצֹצְר֥וֹת הַתְּרוּעָ֖ה לְהָרִ֣יעַ עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אַל־תִּלָּֽחֲמ֛וּ עִם־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֖ם כִּי־לֹ֥א תַצְלִֽיחוּ׃
records.gloss: And look, with us at the head [is] the God, and his priests, and [the] trumpets of the battle cry to sound against you. Sons of Israel, do not fight with Yahweh [the] God of your fathers, for not you will succeed.
pieces: Look, God is with us at our head, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} priests are here with their trumpets to sound the battle call against you. Israelites, do not fight against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors, for you will not succeed."

L.12: And look, God [is] with us at the head, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} priests and the trumpets of the battle cry, to sound the battle cry against you. Sons of Israel, do not fight against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of your fathers, for you will not succeed."

R.12: God is with us and leads us. His priests are here with their trumpets, ready to sound the signal for battle against you. Israelites, do not fight against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors. You will not win!"

decisions.choice: God with us at our head: God leads Judah's army
decisions.reason: Abijah pictures God as the commander who goes before his army, as Yahweh went before Israel (Deuteronomy 20:1-4; Judges 4:14). The priests with him show that the battle is his.

decisions.choice: the trumpets of the battle cry: the signal the Law gave the priests
decisions.reason: The Law told the priests to sound the trumpets for war, "and you will be remembered before Yahweh your God and saved from your enemies" (Numbers 10:9; compare 31:6). Abijah's priests carry out that command.

decisions.choice: do not fight against Yahweh
decisions.reason: Because the kingdom of Judah is Yahweh's kingdom (verse 8), fighting it is fighting Yahweh himself. Abijah appeals to the northern tribes as worshipers of the same God, "the God of your fathers".

decisions.choice: Israelites
decisions.reason: The "sons of Israel" here are the soldiers of the northern army facing Judah. Literal keeps "sons of Israel"; Balanced and Readable say "Israelites". No inclusive alternative is offered, since the words are addressed to an army.

decisions.choice: "look" left out; a short closing sentence
decisions.reason: Readable leaves out "look" and ends with a short sentence, "You will not win!", for the reason Abijah gives.

records.source: וְיָֽרָבְעָ֗ם הֵסֵב֙ אֶת־הַמַּאְרָ֔ב לָב֖וֹא מֵֽאַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וְהַמַּאְרָ֖ב מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And Jeroboam had caused to go around the ambush to come from behind them, and they were before Judah, and the ambush [was] from behind them.
pieces: Meanwhile Jeroboam had sent an ambush around to come up behind them, so that his army was in front of Judah and the ambush was behind them.

L.13: But Jeroboam had sent the ambush around to come from behind them; so they were in front of Judah, and the ambush [was] behind them.

R.13: Meanwhile Jeroboam had sent some of his soldiers around to attack Judah from behind. So Jeroboam's army was in front of Judah's army, and the men in hiding were behind them.

decisions.choice: Jeroboam had sent: done while Abijah spoke
decisions.reason: The sentence puts Jeroboam first and uses a verb form that steps back from the story: while Abijah was making his appeal, Jeroboam had already moved troops behind Judah's lines.

decisions.choice: they ... them: Jeroboam's main army, and Judah
decisions.reason: "They were before Judah" means Jeroboam's main force faced Judah, and "behind them" means behind Judah's army.

decisions.choice: his army; Jeroboam's army ... Judah's army
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who "they" and "them" are (m2). Readable also says what an ambush is: men hidden to attack from behind.

records.source: וַיִּפְנ֣וּ יְהוּדָ֗ה וְהִנֵּ֨ה לָהֶ֤ם הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ פָּנִ֣ים וְאָח֔וֹר וַֽיִּצְעֲק֖וּ לַיהוָ֑ה וְהַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים מַחְצְרִ֖ים בַּחֲצֹצְרֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And turned Judah, and look, to them [was] the battle front and back. And they cried to Yahweh, and the priests [were] blowing on the trumpets.
pieces: When Judah turned, they saw that the battle was in front of them and behind them. They cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the priests blew the trumpets.

L.14: And Judah turned, and look, the battle [was] before them and behind; and they cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the priests blew on the trumpets.

R.14: The soldiers of Judah turned around and saw that they had enemies in front of them and behind them. They cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help, and the priests blew their trumpets.

decisions.choice: and look: what Judah saw
decisions.reason: The word that often means "look" here shows the scene through the soldiers' eyes: when they turned, they saw they were surrounded.

decisions.choice: cried out to Yahweh: called to him for help
decisions.reason: To cry out to Yahweh is to call on him in danger (Exodus 14:10; Judges 3:9). Judah does what Abijah said they would: they rely on Yahweh (verse 18).

decisions.choice: the priests blew the trumpets: as Abijah had said
decisions.reason: The priests sound the trumpets of verse 12, the signal for war the Law gave them (Numbers 10:9).

decisions.choice: they saw that
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "they saw" for the word "look" (m1). Readable adds "for help" to say why they cried out.

records.source: וַיָּרִ֖יעוּ אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיְהִ֗י בְּהָרִ֨יעַ֙ אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה וְהָאֱלֹהִ֗ים נָגַ֤ף אֶת־יָֽרָבְעָם֙ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִפְנֵ֥י אֲבִיָּ֖ה וִיהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And raised a shout [the] men of Judah, and it was when shouted [the] men of Judah, and the God struck Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
pieces: Then the men of Judah raised the battle cry. And as they shouted, God struck down Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.

L.15: And the men of Judah raised the battle cry; and it happened, when the men of Judah raised the battle cry, that God struck Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.

R.15: Then the men of Judah gave a loud battle shout. As they shouted, God defeated Jeroboam and the whole army of Israel in front of Abijah and the men of Judah.

decisions.choice: raised the battle cry: the war shout
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for sounding the trumpets in verse 12. Here the soldiers themselves raise the shout, as Israel did at Jericho (Joshua 6:16, 20).

decisions.choice: God struck Jeroboam: God himself won the battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike or rout. The text says God struck the army at the moment of the shout, before any fighting is told: the victory is his.

decisions.choice: the man of Judah: the men of Judah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "man of Judah", a collective word for all the soldiers of Judah.

decisions.choice: the whole army of Israel; the men of Judah
decisions.reason: Readable says "army" and "men" so the reader knows the peoples are their armies in the field.

records.source: וַיָּנ֥וּסוּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּתְּנֵ֥ם אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: And fled [the] sons of Israel from before Judah, and gave them God into their hand.
pieces: The Israelites fled before Judah, and God gave them into Judah's hands.

L.16: And the sons of Israel fled before Judah, and God gave them into their hand.

R.16: The Israelites ran away from the army of Judah, and God let Judah defeat them.

decisions.choice: gave them into their hand: gave Judah victory over them
decisions.reason: To give someone into another's hand is to put him in his power (Joshua 10:30; Judges 3:10).

decisions.choice: Israelites; Judah's hands
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, "sons of Israel" is "Israelites" at Balanced and Readable. They name Judah for "their", since "them" and "their" refer to different armies.

records.source: וַיַּכּ֥וּ בָהֶ֛ם אֲבִיָּ֥ה וְעַמּ֖וֹ מַכָּ֣ה רַבָּ֑ה וַיִּפְּל֤וּ חֲלָלִים֙ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֔ל חֲמֵשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֖לֶף אִ֥ישׁ בָּחֽוּר׃
records.gloss: And struck among them Abijah and his people a striking great, and fell slain from Israel five hundred thousand man chosen.
pieces: Abijah and his troops struck them with a great slaughter, and 500,000 chosen men of Israel fell dead.

L.17: And Abijah and his people struck them with a great striking, and there fell slain from Israel 500,000 chosen men.

R.17: Abijah and his army killed a great many of them. Of Israel's best soldiers, 500,000 were killed.

decisions.choice: his people: his army
decisions.reason: The word for "people" often means an army in the field, as here.

decisions.choice: five hundred thousand: the size of the number
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, the word for "thousand" may name a unit rather than an exact count (see the note at Numbers 1:21).

decisions.choice: slain: killed in battle
decisions.reason: The word means those pierced or fallen in battle.

decisions.choice: his troops; his army
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "his people"; Balanced says "troops" and Readable "army", as these books do for an army in the field.

records.source: וַיִּכָּנְע֥וּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑יא וַיֶּֽאֶמְצוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה כִּ֣י נִשְׁעֲנ֔וּ עַל־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And were humbled [the] sons of Israel at the time the that, and were strong [the] sons of Judah, because they leaned on Yahweh [the] God of their fathers.
pieces: So the Israelites were humbled at that time, and the men of Judah won the day, because they relied on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors.

L.18: And the sons of Israel were humbled at that time, and the sons of Judah were strong, because they leaned on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of their fathers.

R.18: So at that time the Israelites were defeated, and the men of Judah won, because they trusted {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors.

decisions.choice: were humbled: were brought low, subdued
decisions.reason: The verb means to be bowed down or subdued. Chronicles often uses it of humbling oneself before God (7:14; 12:6-7); here it is the defeat of the northern army.

decisions.choice: because they leaned on Yahweh: trust as the cause of victory
decisions.reason: To lean on Yahweh is to rely on him. Chronicles makes this the reason for victory here and again under Asa (14:10; 16:7-8).

decisions.choice: the men of Judah
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sons of Judah"; Balanced and Readable say "men of Judah", since the soldiers are meant.

records.source: וַיִּרְדֹּ֣ף אֲבִיָּה֮ אַחֲרֵ֣י יָרָבְעָם֒ וַיִּלְכֹּ֤ד מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ עָרִ֔ים אֶת־בֵּֽית־אֵל֙ וְאֶת־בְּנוֹתֶ֔יהָ וְאֶת־יְשָׁנָ֖ה וְאֶת־בְּנוֹתֶ֑יהָ וְאֶת־עֶפְרַ֖יִן וּבְנֹתֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And pursued Abijah after Jeroboam and captured from him cities: Bethel and its daughters, and Jeshanah and its daughters, and Ephron and its daughters.
pieces: Abijah pursued Jeroboam and took towns from him: Bethel and the villages around it, Jeshanah and its villages, and Ephron and its villages.

L.19: And Abijah pursued Jeroboam and took cities from him: Bethel and its daughters, and Jeshanah and its daughters, and Ephron and its daughters.

R.19: Abijah chased Jeroboam and captured some of his towns: Bethel, Jeshanah and Ephron, along with the villages around them.

decisions.choice: its daughters: the villages around a town
decisions.reason: The smaller places that belonged to a town are called its "daughters" (Numbers 21:25; Joshua 15:45).

decisions.choice: Bethel and Jeshanah: towns on the border
decisions.reason: Bethel was one of the two places where Jeroboam set up a golden calf (1 Kings 12:29), so its capture fulfils Abijah's words about the calves. Jeshanah and Ephron lay to the north of it, in the border country between the two kingdoms.

decisions.choice: Ephron: the town's name is uncertain
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has Ephron, and the reading tradition has Ephrain. The town may be the Ophrah of Benjamin (Joshua 18:23) or the place near Ephraim named in 2 Samuel 13:23. The name the written text gives is kept.

decisions.choice: with its villages; the villages around them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "daughters" means here (m1). Readable lists the three towns once and then their villages.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־עָצַ֧ר כֹּֽחַ־יָרָבְעָ֛ם ע֖וֹד בִּימֵ֣י אֲבִיָּ֑הוּ וַיִּגְּפֵ֥הוּ יְהוָ֖ה וַיָּמֹֽת׃פ
records.gloss: And not retained strength Jeroboam again in [the] days of Abijah, and struck him Yahweh, and he died.
pieces: Jeroboam did not regain his power during the days of Abijah. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} struck him, and he died.

L.20: And Jeroboam did not retain strength again in the days of Abijah; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck him, and he died.

R.20: Jeroboam never became strong again while Abijah was alive. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} struck him down, and he died.

decisions.choice: did not retain strength again: never recovered his power
decisions.reason: To "retain strength" is to keep or regain power (compare 22:9). After this defeat Jeroboam did not recover in Abijah's lifetime.

decisions.choice: struck him and he died: Jeroboam, at a later time
decisions.reason: "Him" is Jeroboam, the subject of the sentence. His death came after Abijah's: Jeroboam reigned twenty-two years (1 Kings 14:20), and Asa became king in his twentieth year (1 Kings 15:9). The verse looks ahead to the end of Jeroboam's life.

decisions.choice: Yahweh struck him: his death was a judgment
decisions.reason: The same verb was used for God striking his army (verse 15). Kings says only that Jeroboam lay down with his fathers (1 Kings 14:20); Chronicles names Yahweh as the one who ended his life, as he had ended his army's power.

records.source: וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֣ק אֲבִיָּ֔הוּ וַיִּ֨שָּׂא־ל֔וֹ נָשִׁ֖ים אַרְבַּ֣ע עֶשְׂרֵ֑ה וַיּ֗וֹלֶד עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּשְׁנַ֨יִם֙ בָּנִ֔ים וְשֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה בָּנֽוֹת׃ס
records.gloss: And strengthened himself Abijah, and took for himself wives fourteen, and fathered twenty and two sons and sixteen daughters.
pieces: But Abijah grew strong. He took fourteen wives and had twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.

L.21: But Abijah grew strong, and he took for himself fourteen wives and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.

R.21: But Abijah became more and more powerful. He married fourteen wives and had twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.

decisions.choice: Abijah grew strong: set against Jeroboam's weakness
decisions.reason: The verb for gaining strength is the one used of Jeroboam's men and of Rehoboam in verse 7. Now Abijah is the strong one, while Jeroboam never recovers (verse 20).

decisions.choice: fourteen wives, twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters: a sign of strength
decisions.reason: Many wives and children marked a king's power and God's blessing in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 14:3; 2 Chronicles 11:21). The list may cover his whole life, not only the time after the battle.

decisions.choice: took fourteen wives; married; had ... sons
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "had" for "fathered"; Readable says "married" for "took for himself".

records.heading: The end of Abijah's reign

records.source: וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אֲבִיָּ֔ה וּדְרָכָ֖יו וּדְבָרָ֑יו כְּתוּבִ֕ים בְּמִדְרַ֖שׁ הַנָּבִ֥יא עִדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Abijah, and his ways and his words, [are] written in [the] midrash of the prophet Iddo.
pieces: The rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways and his words, are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo.

L.22: And the rest of the matters of Abijah, and his ways and his words, [are] written in the midrash of the prophet Iddo.

R.22: Everything else Abijah did and said is written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo.

decisions.choice: midrash: a written study or account
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to seek or to study, and is used only here and in 24:27. It probably names a written work that told and explained the history of the kings. It is not the later Jewish writings on Scripture that came to bear the same name. It may simply mean a record or a story.

decisions.choice: the sources formula: in place of 1 Kings 15:7
decisions.reason: Kings sends the reader to "the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah" (1 Kings 15:7). Chronicles names a work by the prophet Iddo instead, as it did for Rehoboam (12:15), and adds "his ways and his words".

decisions.choice: his ways and his words: what he did and what he said
decisions.reason: "Ways" are a person's conduct; "words" may be his speeches, such as the one in verses 4-12, or his affairs.

decisions.choice: acts; midrash (Literal); commentary (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "acts", as in 1 Kings 15:7. Literal keeps the Hebrew word midrash, which is not a common English word. Balanced and Readable call the work a "commentary": a written work that set out and explained the history (m1). The same wording is used for the second source of this name at 24:27.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב אֲבִיָּ֜ה עִם־אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַיִּקְבְּר֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔יד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָסָ֥א בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּ֑יו בְּיָמָ֛יו שָׁקְטָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ עֶ֥שֶׂר שָׁנִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: And lay down Abijah with his fathers, and they buried him in [the] city of David, and reigned Asa his son in his place. In his days was quiet the land ten years.
pieces: Then Abijah rested with his ancestors and was buried in the City of David. His son Asa became king in his place. In his days the land had peace for ten years.

L.23: And Abijah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David, and Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days the land was quiet ten years.

R.23: Then Abijah died and was buried in the City of David. His son Asa became king after him. While Asa was king, the land had peace for ten years.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: the Hebrew text ends chapter 13 here
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text this verse closes chapter 13, and chapter 14 begins with Asa's reforms. Many Bibles number this verse 14:1, and so number the verses of chapter 14 (14:1-14 here) 14:2-15. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: the death formula as in 1 Kings 15:8
decisions.reason: The first part of the verse repeats 1 Kings 15:8 word for word, with Chronicles' form of the name. The last sentence, on the ten years of peace, is found only in Chronicles.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The death formula of Kings and Chronicles (1 Kings 15:8; 2 Chronicles 12:16).

decisions.choice: in his days the land was quiet: Asa's days
decisions.reason: "His days" are Asa's, as chapter 14 goes on to tell (14:4-5). A quiet land is one at peace, free from war (Judges 3:11).

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died; was quiet / had peace
decisions.reason: The death formula is worded as in 1 Kings 15:8 at each level, and "the land was quiet" as in Judges: Literal "was quiet", Balanced and Readable "had peace". Readable names Asa for "his days" (m4).
